event: Hurricane Ian's storm surge on Fort Myers Beach (Estero Island), Florida

minuteZero.what: Lee County orders mandatory evacuation of Zone A (Fort Myers Beach is in Zone A), parts of Zone B and all mobile and manufactured homes.
minuteZero.why: It is the first mandatory order covering the island, so it is when a coordinator would start calling. The Town had only urged high-risk residents to leave on 26 September.

events.what: NHC Storm Surge Warning covering Fort Myers Beach (2100 UTC 26 Sep).
Mandatory evacuation: Zone A, parts of Zone B, mobile and manufactured homes.
Order expanded to all of Zones A and B.
Order expanded to parts of Zone C (WGCU reported 'around 4 p.m.').
County emergency text asks residents to seek shelter or shelter in place by 8:00 p.m.
Shelter-in-place time from the 18:30 text: evacuation travel is meant to be over.
Camera on Estero Blvd, under 0.5 mi from the pier sensor: onset of storm surge inundating the streets (approximate local time).
Same camera: rapidly moving water carrying large floating debris.
Same camera: a home floats off its foundation.
Peak wave-filtered water level at the Fort Myers Beach pier sensor FLLEE03382: 13.23 ft (4.03 m) NAVD88, 12.70 ft above MHHW.
Ian makes landfall on Cayo Costa at 130 kt, 941 mb (1905 UTC), about 30 km north-west of the pier.
Matanzas Pass sensor FLLEE03284 peaks at 12.06 ft (3.68 m) NAVD88.
Big Carlos Pass sensor FLLEE03288 peaks at 3.51 m (11.50 ft) NAVD88 (peak summary says 15:50; the record's maximum is 15:34).
Punta Rassa sensor FLLEE03246 (San Carlos Bay, north-west of the map) peaks at 2.69 m (8.83 ft) NAVD88.
County text urges anyone with water entering their home to go to the highest level possible.
Mullock Creek sensor FLLEE03287 (Estero Bay mainland shore, east of the map) peaks at 3.16 m NAVD88.
Camera: receding water reveals a barren landscape.
Pier sensor back at its dry reading (0.44 m NAVD88).

outcome.deaths: 21 names read at the Town's first-anniversary memorial (News-Press, 28 Sep 2023); 36 of Ian's 41 US surge deaths were in Lee County (NHC TCR p. 12). No official count by cause for Estero Island.
